tech.name: Google Antigravity /swarm (Swarm)
tech.status: preview; all plans, Antigravity App and CLI (business and enterprise accounts when the admin allows); uses quota much faster than a single conversation
tech.one_line: /swarm turns your conversation into a coordinator that splits a task across named worker agents working at the same time, usually adds a verifier that runs the tests and reports problems to the worker that wrote the code, and has them all post on one shared board you can watch.
tech.released_note: v2.31.0 (App) November 9, 2026; business and enterprise accounts from v2.33.0, November 17, 2026, when the admin allows

predecessor.name: One agent in a single conversation working through the task (the default agent); our scene: you check and test each change yourself

hook.text: Antigravity Swarm: you think 3 separate files cost you 3 waits, but actually 3 agents code them at once, and usually another tests them before you look.

claims.text: 'runs a team of named agents that split your task, work on the pieces at the same time'
'when you want a second agent to review and test the changes before you see them'
The 3 files are the maker's example: 'Add input validation to the three API handlers ... Give each handler its own worker ... have a verifier run npm test'
'The coordinator usually adds a @verifier for every two to four workers.'

before.text: Here's what changed. Before, one agent took users, orders and products in turn; after each, you ran the tests yourself.

claims.text: Our scene of the default single agent: 'For everyday coding and quick questions, prompt the default agent directly.' / 'a single conversation'; not a maker's claim about speed

new.text: Now, in preview, you type /swarm, and your chat becomes the coordinator: it gives each file its own worker, at the same time, plus, usually, a verifier that runs the tests and sends problems back to the coder. They all talk on one shared board you can watch: questions, test results.

claims.text: 'your current conversation becomes the swarm's coordinator'
'adds a named worker for each piece' (one worker per file or per package)
'The coordinator usually adds a @verifier for every two to four workers. The verifier reads the diffs, runs the tests, and reports problems to the worker that wrote the code, which then fixes them.'
'Assignments, questions between workers, diff summaries, and test results are posted to the shared board'
'Click it to open the live Swarm pane in the side panel.'
v2.31.0, November 9, 2026: 'You can now use /swarm to coordinate multiple subagents over a message board to complete long-horizon tasks.'

why.text: The catch: it works best when a task splits cleanly, and it uses your quota much faster.

claims.text: 'Use it when a task divides cleanly across separate files, packages, or questions'
'Every worker is its own agent, so a swarm uses quota much faster than a single conversation.'
'available on all plans across the Google Antigravity App and the Antigravity CLI (on business and enterprise accounts, when allowed by organization admin settings)'

takeaway.text: So, what we learned: 3 files used to mean 3 waits; now, when the task splits, 3 agents take them at once, and usually a verifier tests first.

claims.text: The 3 waits are our illustration, not a maker's number; the maker gives no speed-up or time saved
